en.q:
The following are the stages of life cycle of Plasmodium. Arrange the stages in the proper order :
A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells.

B. परजीवी यकृत कोशिकाओं में अलैंगिक जनन करते हैं, कोशिकाओं को फोड़कर रुधिर में मुक्त होते हैं।
C. लाल रुधिर कणिकाओं (RBC) में युग्मकजनक विकसित होते हैं।
D. जीवाणुज रुधिर द्वारा यकृत तक पहुँचते हैं।
E. मादा मच्छर काटते समय मनुष्य में जीवाणुज डालती है।
नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :

en.q:
Match List I with List II :
List-I (Drug) — List-II (Effect)
A. Nicotine — I. Causes sense of euphoria and increased energy
B. Morphine — II. Stimulates adrenal gland to release catecholamines into blood circulation
C. Heroin — III. Effective sedative and painkiller
D. Cocaine — IV. A depressant; slows down body function
en.sol:
• A Nicotine — stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline and noradrenaline (catecholamines) into blood (II).
  • B Morphine — very effective sedative and painkiller (III).
  • C Heroin — a depressant, slows down body functions (IV).
  • D Cocaine — interferes with dopamine transport; gives euphoria and increased energy (I).

A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

सूची I का सूची II से मिलान कीजिए :
सूची-I (औषध) — सूची-II (प्रभाव)

en.q: The overall ability of the host to fight disease-causing organisms, conferred by the immune system, is called immunity. Its two types, as classified in NCERT, are:
en.sol: NCERT 7.2: we meet many infectious agents daily but only a few cause disease, because the body defends itself. This ability, conferred by the immune system, is immunity, of two types: innate (non-specific, present at birth) and acquired (pathogen-specific, with memory). Active/passive, humoral/cell-mediated and primary/secondary responses are subdivisions or features of acquired immunity.
en.hint: Born with it vs gained later.
en.trap: Active and passive are kinds of acquired immunity, not the two main types.

en.q: Which of the following is not listed in NCERT as a factor that motivates adolescents towards drug and alcohol use?
o: Curiosity, need for adventure and excitement, and experimentation
Stress from pressure to excel in academics or examinations
The perception that smoking or using drugs is 'cool' or progressive
Parenting that combines high levels of nurturance with consistent discipline
en.sol: NCERT 7.5.1: adolescence (about 12–18 years) is a vulnerable phase. Causes listed are curiosity, adventure, excitement and experimentation; academic and examination stress; the perception that it is 'cool' or progressive (promoted by television, movies, newspapers, internet); unstable or unsupportive family structures; and peer pressure. Parenting with high nurturance and consistent discipline is, by contrast, associated with a lowered risk of substance abuse (NCERT 7.5.4).
en.hint: One option protects rather than pushes.

en.q: The tendency of the body to show a characteristic and unpleasant withdrawal syndrome (anxiety, shakiness, nausea, sweating) when a regular dose of drugs or alcohol is abruptly stopped is called:
en.sol: NCERT 7.5.2: dependence is the body's tendency to manifest a withdrawal syndrome when the regular dose is abruptly discontinued; it is relieved when use is resumed. en.trap: Addiction is the psychological pull; dependence is the body's withdrawal reaction.

en.q: According to NCERT, which approach helps in the prevention and control of drug and alcohol abuse among adolescents?
o: Pushing the child to perform beyond his/her threshold limits in studies and sports
Waiting until the habit is established before seeking professional help
Identifying situations that may push an adolescent towards drugs early, avoiding undue peer pressure, and parenting with high nurturance and consistent discipline
en.sol: NCERT 7.5.4: 'prevention is better than cure'. Habits are most often taken up during adolescence, so situations that push an adolescent towards drugs or alcohol should be identified and remedied in time; parents and teachers have a special responsibility. Parenting combining high nurturance and consistent discipline lowers the risk of substance abuse, and undue peer pressure should be avoided — a child should not be pushed beyond his/her threshold limits.
